page: Microsoft Azure M16-8ms is an x86_64 memory-intensive virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8280M processor with 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs running at 2.7 GHz. The server is equipped with 438.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 54.69 GB per core. Local storage consists of a 524 GB SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data reveals a clear tradeoff between massive memory capacity and processing speed. The single-core and multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the bottom 10% and bottom 25% respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show weak read performance for both small and large blocks, though large block write bandwidth achieves an average rating. Cryptographic and compression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3 operations, also perform in the lower percentiles.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance provides high memory density relative to its compute footprint, making it suitable for workloads that require large datasets to reside entirely in memory but do not demand intense CPU throughput. Appropriate workloads include large-scale in-memory databases, caching layers, and memory-heavy enterprise applications where memory capacity is the primary bottleneck rather than raw processing power.
